title: A platform cuts the approved ad short
when: A platform shortens an approved ad to fit its limits.
steps: Agent 12 (Marketing Campaign) treats the shortened version as an edit.
It sends the shortened text back to Compliance (Agent 17) for review, as it would any new copy.
never: Run a shortened ad on the strength of the full version's approval.
why: Cutting text can change its meaning or drop a required disclosure. What runs is what must be approved.
you_see: The shortened text going through Compliance again.
test: A live listing's ad is cut by the platform to "3 bedrooms, 2 bathrooms, 1800 sq ft...".

title: A platform rejects an ad
when: An advertising platform rejects an ad.
steps: Agent 12 records the rejection exactly as the platform gave it.
It tells you, and does not change the targeting to get past the filter.
never: Adjust targeting or wording just to get past a platform's filter.
why: Housing ads have special rules on most platforms. Working around a rejection can turn into illegal targeting.
you_see: A question with the platform's rejection.
test: Facebook rejects an ad: "AD_REJECTED: housing category requires special ad category".

title: Engagement numbers disagree between sources
when: Different sources report different engagement numbers for the same listing.
steps: Agent 12 reports both, each named with its source.
It records the conflict and asks you.
why: Numbers you show a seller must be traceable. Two named sources let you explain the difference.
you_see: A question saying engagement numbers conflict, with both sources.
test: Facebook reports engagement 40 and Zillow reports 55 for the same listing. (Today the agent keeps one figure per platform, so the same platform reporting twice replaces the first figure: listed as a finding in the test file.)

title: It is not clear the listing may be marketed yet
when: The listing's status under the Clear Cooperation rule is unclear (not confirmed active on the MLS, and no exemption on file).
steps: Agent 12 publishes nothing.
The approved ad waits at the gate.
never: Publish marketing before the listing is cleared to be marketed.
why: Marketing a listing publicly before it is on the MLS can break the MLS's Clear Cooperation rule and bring fines.
test: A new listing whose go-live you have not authorized: the description is approved, but the MLS never confirms it active.

title: An ad idea ties into a trending topic
when: A campaign is built around a trending topic or current event.
steps: Agent 12 asks you to approve the idea before anything else happens.
The copy is not sent for review until you approve.
never: Run a trending-topic tie-in without your approval.
why: Trending topics can turn sour fast; your name is on the ad.
you_see: A question about the trending-topic tie-in.
test: A signed campaign "Open house Sunday" marked as a trending-topic tie-in.

title: An ad mentions details not in the listing record
when: An ad refers to specifics that are not in the listing data.
steps: Agent 12 pulls the ad.
never: Let marketing say more than the MLS record.
why: Claims beyond the record are unverified claims in public.

title: The fair housing review is still pending
when: An ad or listing copy is waiting for Compliance's verdict.
steps: Nothing publishes while the verdict is pending.
The verdict is a gate, not a race: no deadline lets copy through without it.
why: Fair housing violations in ads bring complaints and fines. Review comes first, every time.
you_see: The copy waiting for review; nothing published.
test: No compliance rules are loaded, so Agent 17 returns no verdict: both the listing description and a new "Open house Sunday" campaign wait, and nothing publishes.

title: A campaign asks to target people by age or other demographics
when: A campaign's settings include demographic targeting (for example an age range).
steps: Agent 12 refuses it outright.
It raises a legal-line alert for you.
The campaign is not sent for review or run.
never: Target housing ads by age, family status or any protected characteristic.
why: Demographic targeting of housing ads is illegal under fair housing law. Geography is allowed under farm rules; people are not.
you_see: A legal-line alert about demographic targeting.
test: A signed campaign targeting ages 25 to 40.

title: A published ad turns out to be out of date
when: An ad already running is found to be wrong (for example the price changed on the MLS).
steps: Agent 12 records what changed.
It prepares the retraction the same day; the retraction is held for your signed release.
It tells you the retraction is waiting for you.
never: Leave a known-wrong ad running without telling you.
why: A wrong price in public is a misrepresentation. It must be fixed the same day.
you_see: A question saying the retraction is held for your signed release.
test: A live listing's ad is found stale: price $450,000 became $439,000 on the MLS.

title: Someone changes the marketing budget by word of mouth
when: A budget change is reported verbally.
steps: Agent 12 records the report.
The budget you signed stays in force until you sign a new figure.
never: Change the budget on someone's word.
why: Spending your money is your signed decision.
test: You signed a budget of $500. A report that "seller said go to 800" arrives.

title: Compliance flags campaign copy
steps: Agent 12 publishes nothing.
It tells you, with Compliance's findings (the phrase and the rule).
It waits for your corrected, signed copy.
never: Publish flagged copy, or rewrite it on its own.
why: The fix to fair housing language is yours to make and sign.
you_see: A question with the flagged phrase and the rule it broke.
test: A campaign says "Perfect for young families near the park"; Compliance flags it under rule FH-1.
